gaps.concept: SRY activates SOX9, which drives Sertoli cell differentiation and testis cord formation.
gaps.why_tested: An SRY-positive embryo has a SOX9 defect and fails to develop testes.

gaps.concept: SRY translocation onto the X chromosome can produce a 46,XX individual with testes and a male phenotype.
gaps.why_tested: A phenotypic male has a 46,XX karyotype and an SRY-positive X chromosome.

gaps.concept: Complete 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis (Swyer syndrome) causes streak gonads, a uterus, female external genitalia, and absent spontaneous puberty.
gaps.why_tested: Primary amenorrhea and little breast development occur in an adolescent with a uterus and 46,XY karyotype.

gaps.concept: Complete androgen insensitivity is an X-linked androgen receptor defect: 46,XY, testes, absent uterus, blind vagina, breasts, and scant pubic hair.
gaps.why_tested: Primary amenorrhea with breasts, scant pubic hair, and inguinal testes must be distinguished from Müllerian agenesis.

gaps.concept: Androgen insensitivity typically produces male-range or elevated testosterone and elevated LH because androgen-mediated negative feedback is impaired.
gaps.why_tested: Hormone results distinguish androgen resistance from impaired testosterone synthesis in a 46,XY patient.

gaps.concept: Partial androgen insensitivity can cause ambiguous genitalia, severe hypospadias, and pubertal gynecomastia.
gaps.why_tested: A 46,XY adolescent with hypospadias and gynecomastia has residual androgen receptor activity.

gaps.concept: Autosomal recessive SRD5A2 deficiency causes undervirilized external genitalia despite testes, Wolffian structures, and Müllerian regression; virilization occurs at puberty.
gaps.why_tested: A child raised as female develops a deeper voice and phallic enlargement at puberty.

gaps.concept: 5α-reductase deficiency produces a high testosterone-to-DHT ratio and usually lacks the pubertal gynecomastia characteristic of partial androgen insensitivity.
gaps.why_tested: Hormone results and pubertal findings distinguish two causes of 46,XY undervirilization.

gaps.concept: AMH or AMH-receptor defects cause persistent Müllerian duct syndrome: a phenotypic male retains a uterus and may have cryptorchidism.
gaps.why_tested: A uterus is discovered during surgery for an undescended testis in a 46,XY child.

gaps.concept: Prenatal androgen excess from 21-hydroxylase deficiency virilizes 46,XX external genitalia while ovaries and Müllerian internal structures remain intact.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn has ambiguous external genitalia, no palpable testes, and a uterus.

gaps.concept: Placental aromatase deficiency can virilize both a 46,XX fetus and the pregnant mother.
gaps.why_tested: Maternal hirsutism accompanies ambiguous genitalia in a 46,XX newborn.

gaps.concept: Placental hCG stimulates fetal Leydig cell testosterone production during male sexual differentiation.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which placental hormone supports fetal androgen production.

gaps.concept: INSL3 promotes transabdominal testicular descent; androgen signaling supports subsequent passage through the inguinal canal into the scrotum.
gaps.why_tested: A defect in a descent signal leaves testes undescended despite otherwise normal duct development.

gaps.concept: Cryptorchidism is more common with prematurity and increases infertility and testicular germ cell tumor risk.
gaps.why_tested: An undescended inguinal testis is linked to later impaired fertility or malignancy.

gaps.concept: During inguinal descent, testes acquire internal spermatic fascia from transversalis fascia, cremasteric fascia from internal oblique, and external spermatic fascia from external oblique.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which abdominal wall layer supplies a spermatic cord covering.

gaps.concept: Failed processus vaginalis closure causes communicating hydrocele, a usually painless, transilluminating scrotal swelling.
gaps.why_tested: A newborn’s scrotal swelling transilluminates and communicates with the peritoneal cavity.

gaps.concept: A patent processus vaginalis also permits congenital indirect inguinal hernia, with bowel entering the scrotum through the deep inguinal ring.
gaps.why_tested: A reducible infant scrotal mass contains bowel instead of hydrocele fluid.

gaps.concept: Mesonephric tubules form efferent ductules connecting the rete testis to the epididymis.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks the embryologic origin of the ducts between testis and epididymis.

gaps.concept: The appendix testis is a Müllerian remnant; its torsion can produce a tender blue-dot sign.
gaps.why_tested: A child with acute scrotal pain has a blue spot near the superior testicular pole.

gaps.concept: The urogenital sinus gives rise to prostatic and bulbourethral gland epithelium in males and vestibular and paraurethral gland epithelium in females.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks the embryologic source of accessory genital gland epithelium.

gaps.concept: Most male urethral epithelium derives from urogenital sinus endoderm; distal glanular urethral epithelium derives from surface ectoderm.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which embryologic tissue forms the distal penile urethra.

gaps.concept: A septate uterus has a normal outer fundal contour; a bicornuate uterus has a deep external fundal cleft.
gaps.why_tested: Pelvic imaging shows two uterine cavities, requiring distinction between failed septum resorption and failed duct fusion.

gaps.concept: Uterus didelphys commonly has two cervices and may have a longitudinal vaginal septum.
gaps.why_tested: Examination finds duplicated cervices alongside two separate uterine cavities.

gaps.concept: A unicornuate uterus results from absent or arrested development of one Müllerian duct and may include a rudimentary horn.
gaps.why_tested: Imaging shows one uterine horn with a small contralateral remnant.

gaps.concept: Gartner duct cysts occur along the anterolateral vaginal wall.
gaps.why_tested: A vaginal wall cyst must be identified by its location and Wolffian origin.

gaps.concept: Imperforate hymen reflects failed hymenal canalization; transverse vaginal septum reflects failed fusion or canalization between vaginal components.
gaps.why_tested: An obstructed vagina has cyclic pain, but examination distinguishes a bulging hymen from a higher vaginal septum.

gaps.concept: Vaginal atresia can result from failed development or canalization of the sinovaginal bulbs.
gaps.why_tested: A patient has congenital lower vaginal absence despite developed Müllerian structures.

gaps.concept: Fetal exposure to 5α-reductase inhibitors such as finasteride can impair development of male external genitalia.
gaps.why_tested: A medication exposure during pregnancy is linked to undervirilized genitalia in a male fetus.
